newsitem.title: UK: IPE GAS OIL SEEN $2-$2.50 LOWER, BRENT UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: IPE GAS OIL SEEN $2-$2.50 LOWER, BRENT UNCHANGED.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open $2-$2.50 a tonne lower on Monday, catching up with a weak close on Brent crude which is due unchanged, brokers said.
"Gas oil is due $2 lower against Brent and $3 lower against (NYMEX) heating oil but we don't think it will go that far," said a broker.
August gas oil, which expires at midday on Tuesday, settled at $169.50 a tonne on Friday. Dealers pegged technical support on the September contract at $169 and then $166 a tonne.
Sept Brent ended 42 cents weaker at $18.48 a barrel after the U.N. gave Iraq the green light to resume limited exports.
Brokers said Brent could win a short reprieve after tumbling from a 10-week high of $19.64 a barrel last Monday but the outlook remained weak.
"Brent could spark up on a bit of profit-taking but it won't be long before it has another go at the downside," said one.
Baghdad is expected to resume crude exports later this week under the terms of the U.N. oil-for-food deal for the first time since late May.
Iraq's pricing formula for oil exports in the second phase of the deal, which runs to December, was given formal Security Council approval on Friday.
The Middle East Economic Survey said on Monday Iraq planned to export about 25-30 million barrels of oil in what remains of the first 90-day period to September 5.
Also continuing to weigh on crude prices were weak refined product markets on both sides of the Atlantic, dealers said.
